newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil council to discuss ports selloff on Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Brazil council to discuss ports selloff on Sept 24.

text.p: Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND) will discuss the privatization of ports at its next meeting on September 24, said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir on Monday.

In June, the CND included 31 ports in the country's privatization program. The federal government is expected to auction concessions to operate the ports of Porto Velho, Laguna, Cabedelo and Itajai. The remaining 27 ports, including Santos and Rio de Janeiro ports, will be offered to private investors under leasehold agreements.

Kandir reiterated his estimates for 10 billion reals in revenue from the privatization of mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and the power sector in 1997. For 1996, privatization revenues are expected to total 3.6 billion reais, Kandir told reporters after a meeting with businessmen promoted by the Brazil-Germany Chamber of Commerce.

He also noted improvements in Brazil's foreign accounts. He said he expects the country's current account deficit to be around 2.0 percent of the gross domestic product this year. Kandir said most of the deficit has been financed by foreign investment, which reached $5.0 billion in the first half.
